name: KÁRYYN at Tonelab
Description:
Tonelab is super excited to host KÁRYYN - a Syrian-Armenian-American vocalist, composer, and producer from Los Angeles. Her music blends operatic vocals, modular synthesis, and deep listening with themes of quantum physics, lineage, and Eastern philosophy. ✨

Her critically acclaimed debut, The Quanta Series (2019), established her reputation as a highly original sonic architect, drawing praise from avant-garde luminaries like Björk, Brian Eno and Marina Abramović.

She returned in 2026 with her new album, Physics Universal Love Language (PULL). Co-produced with James Ford and Hudson Mohawke, the record incorporates traditional Armenian and Middle Eastern instrumentation, blending soaring orchestral strings with gravitational, hypnotic beats. 💫

As if we weren't excited enough already — Shhau will be opening the night with a DJ set 🔥

@shhau.then is a music producer, composer, and sound designer from Yerevan, Armenia. His rhythmic foundation is a defining element of his work, shaping the intricate grooves and layered textures found throughout his productions. With a background in music theory and sound design, Shhau's approach is both technically refined and artistically versatile. He has been an active figure in Yerevan's dynamic music scene, particularly at the crossroads of electronic, jazz, and experimental genres.

name: Curatorial Tour of Anna Boghiguian's 'Weaving Culture'
Description:
Join us for a curatorial tour of Anna Boghiguian's exhibition "Weaving Culture" with Nairi Khatchadourian, on Saturday at 11am at the National Gallery of Armenia.

What new perspectives on weaving culture the artist narrates through her series of 37 handmade carpets and tapestries? How did the collaboration with displaced women weavers from Artsakh contribute to experimenting new weaving and dyeing techniques, engaging with a new artistic vocabulary, and cultivating, in the weavers' new environments, a renewed sense of collectiveness?

The curatorial tour will bring insights into the 'Weaving Culture' residency, the drawing to carpet translation process, and the human histories and material culture interwoven throughout Anna Boghiguian's artistic practice.

Language: Armenian

Visual: Anna Boghiguian, «Bird Transforms into Angel and Vice Versa», ink on paper, 2025.

name: Book Presentation: "The Armenian Churches of Iran" by Sherly Avedian
Description:
Updated date‼️
On Friday, May 29 at 19:00, as part of the fifth month [May] of the new season of "12 Months," Library for Architecture will host Sherly Avedian @avedashen, in collaboration with the month's curator, @storaket_architectural_studio, for a book presentation and discussion exploring this month's theme: "Values and Belongings."

The selected book is "The Armenian Churches of Iran" by Sherly Avedian.

Today, 123 Armenian churches remain standing in Iran. These structures reflect not only religious heritage, but also a broader narrative of cultural endurance and transformation. The research and documentation on this architectural legacy have been brought together in this book, offering a comprehensive reading of its place within both regional and global cultural history.

During the presentation and discussion on the book and the preservation of Armenian churches in Iran, the author will share insights into their historical significance, architectural value, and their place within the broader discourse of world heritage.

Book language: Armenian, English
Discussion language: Armenian

name: 14 CONCEPT — STRATUMISM by Armen Ronov
Description:
ArAr Gallery presents
14 CONCEPT — STRATUMISM
by @armenronov

Armen Ronov (American, born in Armenia, now based in Italy) is the founder of Stratumism — a conceptual artistic language rooted in geological memory, primordial matter, and the physical origins of life itself.

The series explores the moment where magma becomes flesh, where form emerges from lava, heat, minerals, and elemental chaos.

Created through linen canvas, lava-derived pigments, precious stones, meteorite alloys, and handcrafted mineral paints developed by the artist himself, the works exist somewhere between painting, landscape, and ritual object.

At the center of the series is the body as both canvas and planetary surface — a living texture carrying traces of time, movement, pain, and transformation.

The presented works belong to a strictly limited body of work existing beyond human temporality — as if already belonging to geological time itself.

—
14 works by Armen Ronov are currently presented by ArAr Gallery.

Prices, dimensions, and titles are indicated in the slides.

On the same evening, a special release in collaboration with @o0thing will also be presented.

Selected works are available for acquisition worldwide.

name: Tughtugir Zine Festival
Description:
Dear friends, we are happy to invite you to the three-day zine festival "Tughtugir," organized by FemLibrary, which will take place from May 15 to May 17.

The festival is dedicated to works created with limited resources, documenting, celebrating, and empowering queer and feminist forms of expression through zine-making. It is aimed at zine-makers, visual storytellers, artists, writers, illustrators, and community members. During the exhibition, you will have the chance to discover works by artists from both Armenia and the region.

The exhibited works include poetry, political texts, photographs, comics, and other forms of expression created in experimental formats and with a DIY approach.

A zine (or fanzine) originates from the English word "magazine." In Armenian, ինքնահրատ (inqnahrat) is a non-commercial print or digital publication often produced in small quantities with limited resources. Zines are typically handmade, easily reproducible, and come in various formats such as folded, stitched, or glued booklets. Zines are not expected to be "perfectly made," which allows them to include grammatical mistakes, radical ideas, opinions, critiques, and even typos, giving them a more personal character.

The origins of zine-making can be traced back to amateur press movements of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Their role in preserving and representing underground cultures and marginalized groups makes this art form especially relevant today. Zines have developed as an anarchist tool for sharing ideas and thoughts about political and social issues that matter to people.

*թուղթ (tught) paper + գիր (gir) writing is a reference to the ritual act of writing someone's name or words on paper as part of casting a spell. We approach this tradition through a feminist lens, viewing it not as a source of fear or harm, but recognizing the power of writing itself.

We will also share more details about the festival program soon.

The festival is supported by The Europe Challenge program.

name: Pedro Rodrigues: Guitar | Portugal
Description:
Pedro Rodrigues: Guitar | Portugal
leg On May 12, at 7:30 PM, the Komitas Chamber Music Hall will host a solo recital of the famous Portuguese guitarist Pedro Rodrigues.
The works of Portuguese, Cuban, Italian and Armenian composers will be performed.
•. In the program:
- José Duarte Costa (1921-2004): "Balada da Solidão", "Procissão"- Luiz José Maria Oliveira (1821-1883): "Grandes Variançoens"
- António Pinho Vargas (1951): "Brinquedos", "Tom Waits" (arr. Pedro Rodrigues)
- Saint Grigor Narekatsi (951-1003): "Havun Havun" (arr. Pardy Minassian)
- Edward Mirzoyan (1921-2012): "Tkhoor vals" (arr. Pardy Minassian)
- Traditional: "Ari Im Sokhak" (arr. Pardy Minassian)
- Nuccio d'Angelo (1955): "Due Canzoni Lidie"
- Luís Carvalho (1974): "Arabesco I", "Arabesco II" (World Premiere)
- Leo Brouwer (1939): "Sonata 1"
• Pedro Rodrigues
Winner of the Artist's International Auditions (New York), the Concorso Sor (Rome) and the Prémio Jovens Músicos, as well as a laureate of over twenty competitions including Salieri-Zinetti, Paris, Montélimar, Valencia, and Sernancelhe, Pedro Rodrigues is an Associate Professor at the University of Aveiro, an Integrated Researcher at INET-md, Director of the Master's in Music program, Artistic Director of the UA Autumn Festivals, and a member of the UA General Council.
• He has performed as a soloist in many internationally renowned, and has premiered over 60 works by contemporary composers. His discography includes 19 titles. He is regularly invited to teach masterclasses at universities across Europe, the Americas, Africa, and Asia.
* Tickets price: 3000 - 7000 AMD | https://nccm.am/en/events?id=2792
ENTRY FOR CHILDREN UNDER 6 YEARS OLD IS PROHIBITED.
